contrast_to_present_study: The comparison here holds the coordinate field and recorded data fixed within each refit/frozen pair and changes the fitted receiver-intercept state; it is not a head-to-head accuracy comparison with either cited algorithm.
inserted_latex: Unknown-parameter treatment provides a closer comparison. Li et al.~\cite{ref10} jointly estimate target locations, transmit powers and the path-loss exponent while accounting for anchor-location uncertainty. Yan et al.~\cite{ref11} use variational Bayesian learning to refine the noise model, path-loss exponent and sensor positions for subsequent online localization. Here, the recorded observations, perturbed receiver coordinates, receiver selection, evaluation identities and exponent remain fixed within each pair; only the receiver intercepts are refitted from calibration records or retained at their reference values. This comparison quantifies the calibration-state effect within the fixed WCL implementation, rather than evaluating a new joint estimator. The direction-level reversals and weight and affected-message diagnostics characterize that effect; participation and pivot comparisons retain their separate diagnostic roles.
